sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a house fast in Racine, WI?
sections.html:
Racine owners generally choose between a traditional listing, a for-sale-by-owner sale, and a cash purchase by an investor or home buyer. The right one depends on the condition of the house, whether tenants live there, and how soon you need the money.

  • Traditional listing. You get exposure to buyers using mortgages, along with inspections, appraisals and repair requests. Ask for the commission and all other seller-paid charges in writing.
  • For sale by owner. You handle pricing, showings, the condition report and the deed filing yourself, so budget your own time.
  • Cash purchase. A buyer paying cash can often close without a lender, but you should compare the net amount after fees, the closing date and what repairs the buyer expects.

If renters live in the house, or you know of open code items, read the permit and tenant notes below before you sign anything.

sections.h2: What makes Racine different from other southeast Wisconsin cities?
sections.html:
Racine sits on the Lake Michigan shore at the mouth of the Root River, 22 miles south of Milwaukee and 60 miles north of Chicago. It is the Racine County seat, was incorporated as a village in 1841 and as a city in 1848, and by 2020 was the fifth-largest city in Wisconsin, with 77,816 residents. These facts come from Wikipedia's Racine entry.

Manufacturing built the city, and headquarters of Case IH, Dremel, InSinkErator, Modine Manufacturing and S. C. Johnson & Son are still listed there. Frank Lloyd Wright designed the Johnson Wax Headquarters, and the Old Main Street Historic District is part of the city's preserved core. Bridges across the Root River link neighborhoods, the city draws municipal water from Lake Michigan, and Amtrak's Hiawatha serves Racine County from a station in Sturtevant.

Racine is the most densely settled of the four cities in the Census comparison. The Census Bureau counts 5,028.5 people per square mile on 15.48 square miles of land, and estimates 77,908 residents on July 1, 2025.

sections.html:

sections.h2: Which school district serves a Racine house?
sections.html: The Racine Unified School District administers the city's public schools. Wikipedia describes a district of early education, elementary, K-8, 6-12 and high schools with about 16,000 students, and notes International Baccalaureate and Montessori programs. The district's own site, rusd.org, explains school choice and enrollment. Buyers with children often ask about boundaries and choice options, so point them to the district instead of guessing.

sections.h2: What city permits, rental permits and tenant rules apply in Racine?
sections.html:
The Building Inspection Department administers the city and state building, heating, plumbing, electrical and zoning codes. Its permit page lists applications for roofs, siding, fences, garages and sheds, decks and pergolas, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, razing and an occupancy permit. The Building Department's number is 262-636-9464. Call before closing to ask whether a sale of your house triggers an occupancy permit, and whether any permit from past work is still open.

If your buyer plans to use the house as a short-term rental, the city's Short-Term Rentals page explains that stays under 29 consecutive days fall under the state's tourist rooming house rules. The city requires a permit through its Public Health Department, an annual inspection before any guest stays, and room tax under Racine Ordinance 90-55. The permit year runs from July 1 to June 30, and short-term rentals pay Wisconsin sales tax at 5 percent in Racine, with an exception when taxable sales are under $1,000 in a calendar year. Environmental Health answers questions at 262-636-9203.

If tenants live in the house, the city's rental properties page says landlords should complete a signed check-in and check-out form, tenants have seven days after move-in to report other defects, and a landlord who skips the written procedure loses ground in a dispute over conditions unless a government inspector verified them earlier. Pass those records to your buyer.

sections.h2: What must I disclose, and what do the fee and recording cost?
sections.html:
Under Wis. Stat. 709.02, a seller of a one-to-four-unit home hands the buyer a completed condition report within 10 days after acceptance. The form walks through structural and mechanical systems, environmental matters, wells, septic systems and storage tanks, taxes, special assessments and permits, and land use. A buyer who does not receive it can rescind within two business days after the 10 days run out. If a response changes before the buyer accepts, Wis. Stat. 709.035 calls for an amended report. Court-appointed fiduciaries who never occupied the home, and transfers exempt from the transfer fee, are excused under Wis. Stat. 709.01.

The transfer fee is 30 cents per $100 of value, charged to the grantor under Wis. Stat. 77.22. A $200,000 sale costs $600. The Racine County Register of Deeds charges a flat $30 to record a document, and its real estate forms page lists a checklist that every recorded document must meet:

  • Grantor and grantee named, with the grantor's signature notarized or authenticated
  • A complete legal description and the parcel identification number
  • The name of the person who drafted the document, plus a return address
  • Legible text that follows Wisconsin margin and layout guidelines

The office is at 730 Wisconsin Avenue, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, and accepts documents dropped off, mailed or filed electronically. Call (262) 636-3208 or write rod@racinecounty.gov with questions. A quit claim deed form is posted on the county's page, but have an attorney or title company confirm the right deed for your sale.

faqs.q: What should I do about tenants in a Racine house I am selling?
faqs.a: Start with the lease and ask an attorney how a sale affects it. The city's rental page recommends signed check-in and check-out forms that list the condition of major components, and tenants have seven days to report additional defects. Give your buyer copies, and call the city's Fair Housing Office at 262-636-9595 with questions.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit if my buyer wants to rent the house by the night in Racine?
faqs.a: Yes. Rentals under 29 consecutive days need a Tourist Rooming House permit through the city's Public Health Department, an inspection before the first stay, room tax collection, and Wisconsin sales tax unless the host's taxable sales stay under $1,000 a year. The permit year runs July 1 through June 30.

faqs.q: Who pays the Wisconsin transfer fee on a Racine sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it. Wis. Stat. 77.22 puts the fee on the grantor, and the register of deeds collects it when the deed is recorded. The rate is 30 cents per $100, so $150,000 of value produces a $450 fee.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a house in Racine?
faqs.a: At the Racine County Register of Deeds, 730 Wisconsin Avenue, Racine, WI 53403. You can drop the deed off, mail it, or have a title company file it electronically. The recording fee is a flat $30, and the transfer return must be filed online first.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Racine house I inherited?
faqs.a: Yes, but the paperwork depends on how title passed. A transfer by will, descent or survivorship is exempt from the transfer fee under Wis. Stat. 77.25(11), and Racine County lists a $30 fee to record a Termination of Decedent's Property Interest (HT-110). A court-appointed fiduciary who never lived in the house is excused from the condition report, so confirm your status with the probate court or an attorney.
